notes: Every non-null value comes from a page opened or seen in search results on 2026-11-15. 'asof' is the data date when the source states one, otherwise the access date (2026-11-15) with a note. Conversions: EUR->USD at 1.1142 (EUR/USD close 2026-11-06, poundsterlinglive.com/history/EUR-usd-2026); ETH->USD at ~$2,120 (ETH price 2026-11-10, coinedition.com). Where a market has no drawdown index, a default/failure rate is given in an extra 'default_rate' metric (positive %, annual or cumulative as stated) and max_drawdown is null. trust: report = third-party research/press/law firm; platform = the provider's own page; index = published index figure; estimate = secondary/marketing source or derived.

time_to_sell.text: Most common terms: quarterly redemption on 30-90 days' prior notice; US median redemption frequency is quarterly. Gates of 10-25% of NAV per quarter can stretch this.
time_to_sell.source: Proskauer, Hedge Start: Key Hedge Fund Terms; The Hedge Fund Journal (Redemption Terms)
time_to_sell.note: Law-firm guide, undated page; accessed 2026-11-15.

min_ticket.text: $1M is the common benchmark for established funds; reported range roughly $250k-$1M, elite funds $5M-$25M+. Accredited investor or qualified purchaser status also required.
min_ticket.source: Nasdaq, What Are Typical Investment Minimums in Hedge Funds?
min_ticket.note: Range figures came from several search results (Nasdaq, Kubera, SmartAsset); page date not shown.

max_drawdown.source: AIMA research paper (hedge fund industry maximum drawdown)
max_drawdown.note: AIMA does not name the index in the excerpt (likely HFRI Fund Weighted Composite). HFRI FWC calendar 2008 was -18.3% (HFR via Hedgeweek/Cambridge Associates).

volatility.note: HFR publishes since-1990 standard deviation only in subscriber reports; no public figure found.

exit_cost.text: No fee after lock-up; soft lock-up early redemption fees averaged 3.58% in a 2013 industry terms survey.
exit_cost.source: J.P. Morgan Prime Brokerage 2013 Hedge Fund Terms Analysis
exit_cost.note: Old data; seen via search result summary.

time_to_sell.text: Base hedge fund terms: quarterly with 30-90 days notice. Mean hard lock-up across strategies was 1.05 years (2013); top multi-strategy/quant firms (Citadel, Millennium, DE Shaw) have lengthened terms, with DE Shaw reported on a four-year lockup in 2026.
time_to_sell.source: J.P. Morgan 2013 Hedge Fund Terms Analysis; Proskauer; Hedgeweek (DE Shaw extends redemption timelines)
time_to_sell.note: days_high = 1.05-yr mean lock-up plus one quarterly notice cycle; staggered multi-year share classes at top firms can be far longer.

min_ticket.text: Most hedge funds $250k-$1M; many sought-after funds (Citadel, DE Shaw, Millennium, Two Sigma) require $5M-$10M+ and qualified purchasers. Renaissance Medallion is closed to outsiders.
min_ticket.note: No fund-specific minimums published; page undated.

max_drawdown.source: Cambridge Associates, Does Trend-Following's Recent Struggle Signal That the Strategy Is Structurally Broken? (SG Trend Index)
max_drawdown.note: Proxy: systematic/quant trend (SG Trend Index second-largest drawdown since 2000). No public index for market-making funds. Barclay CTA Index max drawdown -32.54% (Dec 1989 - Dec 2019) per Catalyst Funds.

exit_cost.text: Same structure as hedge funds: no fee after lock-up; soft lock-up early redemption fee averaged 3.58% (2013).
exit_cost.source: J.P. Morgan Prime Brokerage 2013 Hedge Fund Terms Analysis
exit_cost.note: General hedge fund figure applied to quant funds.

time_to_sell.text: Not exchange-listed; no guaranteed secondary market. Issuer may buy back or post indicative bids but is not obliged to; holder may be stuck until maturity.
time_to_sell.source: FINRA, Understanding Structured Notes With Principal Protection
time_to_sell.note: No day count published; depends on issuer buyback.

min_ticket.note: No sourced minimum found (common $1,000 denominations not confirmed by any opened source).

max_drawdown.note: No index; outcome depends on underlying and issuer credit.

exit_cost.text: Embedded costs of roughly 2-8% of principal (not disclosed as a fee) per independent analyses cited by a securities law firm; issuer buyback often quoted at a significant discount to face (FINRA); one source cites a 3-5% issuer buyback spread.
exit_cost.source: Bakhtiari & Harrison, Structured Notes Attorneys; FINRA
exit_cost.note: Figures seen in search summary; law-firm (plaintiff-side) source.

time_to_sell.text: Mintos Secondary Market: sale speed depends on demand and price (discount sells faster); no guarantee of a buyer; cash credited after sale and settlement. Otherwise held to loan maturity.
time_to_sell.source: Mintos Help Center, How can I exit my investments / What's the Secondary Market
time_to_sell.note: Mintos publishes no typical days; liquidity article returned 403.

min_ticket.text: Mintos Notes: EUR 50 minimum per Set on primary market (EUR 1 on secondary). Converted at EUR/USD 1.1142 (2026-11-06).
min_ticket.source: Mintos Help Center, What is the minimum amount that can be invested

max_drawdown.note: No drawdown index for P2P loans; see default_rate.

exit_cost.text: Mintos charges 0.85% on each Secondary Market sale, on the final price after any discount; any discount you set is an extra cost.
exit_cost.source: Mintos Help Center, What are the fees and charges on Mintos

min_ticket.text: BCRED minimum initial investment $2,500 (some broker-dealers higher).

exit_cost.text: Shares held less than one year repurchased at 98% of NAV (2% early repurchase deduction); none after one year.

min_ticket.note: No minimum sourced (gas costs make tiny positions uneconomic).

exit_cost.note: Gas only; no figure sourced. Failed withdrawals at full utilization also cost gas.
